question: Should OpenClaw publish a Swagger/OpenAPI contract for the Gateway, and should it cover only documented HTTP routes or also try to model WebSocket RPC/protocol schemas?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing OpenAPI scope defines a new supported API/discovery contract across security-sensitive Gateway HTTP routes, existing TypeBox JSON Schema generation, and the public client SDK direction.

options.title: Approve static HTTP-only OpenAPI
options.body: Generate a versioned OpenAPI document for documented HTTP routes, include bearer-auth semantics, and leave WebSocket RPC on TypeBox/JSON Schema.

options.title: Defer to TypeBox and SDK surfaces
options.body: Keep the existing protocol JSON Schema and Gateway client/app SDK tracks as the supported programmatic path until maintainers want an HTTP OpenAPI contract.

options.title: Expose runtime Swagger endpoint
options.body: Serve /openapi.json or Swagger UI from the Gateway only after deciding auth, route inclusion, and private-ingress behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve static HTTP-only OpenAPI
recommendation.body: Generate a versioned OpenAPI document for documented HTTP routes, include bearer-auth semantics, and leave WebSocket RPC on TypeBox/JSON Schema.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current routing candidate for Gateway API docs, schema, and client-package direction based on current-main history and adjacent review context.
